liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (3 reviews): Reviewer asks whether anyone has ever heard a bad Bird Song, noting the show's close, comfy vibe; Reviewer's favorite Bird Song of this period, surpassed only by a few, including one from 8/27/72 [17][19][20]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): The opener is so spot-on it feels like a mid-set or second-set opener; the crowd seemed stunned [19]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): One of the most intense versions in a while; the crowd gets amped as it peaks [21]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review): Smokin' hot, with Garcia sounding like he dances over the very strong backing of the band [19]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Rider is dynamite, especially in the solo section; the transition from China Cat is unremarkable [21]

## The recordings

- **gd81-03-03.horvath.cheadle.9113.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has clear vocals and crisp guitars; the band's energy comes through [11]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83828.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Judged the best recording among several available of this show [22]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.wagner.miller.90473.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 165 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [6]
- **gd1981-03-03.139736.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 156 min [2]

## Around the show

- Music Hall is a roughly 2,500-seat room; Jerry's guitar made the room vibrate, and smoking indoors was still allowed [11]
- Reviewer's group tried to tape the show, but a bouncer confiscated their batteries [11]
- Tickets were easy to get; reviewer sat fifth row left, seeing Jerry in a long black shirt with long graying hair [17]
- Taped from the front row center of the balcony [6]
- Reviewer calls it a pretty standard show for the year, which means very good [16]
- Reviewer feels Cleveland tended to bring out the best in the band, this show included [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd81-03-03.horvath.cheadle.9113.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Mark Horvath; transferred by Mark Horvath; source: Audience: Sennheiser 421's [1]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.taylor-radnor.gross.gems.83828.flac16**: taped by Mason Taylor and Mark Radnor; transferred by Todd Evans and Jamie Waddell; source: NAK 700 (shotgun capsules) > Nak 550 Cassette Recorder > Maxell Metal > HHB Porta-a-DAT [5]
- **gd1981-03-03.nak700.wagner.miller.90473.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/Maxell DXLIIS/Dolby B) D [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 cassette master from Bob Wagner's tapes, transferred to CD; same source as shnid 9113 [6]
- **gd1981-03-03.139736.fob.beyer.m88.streeter.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Beyer M88 > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) > Tascam… [2]
